song.title: Another Brick In The Wall, Part 2

guitar.evidence: David Gilmour's "Black Strat" Fender Stratocaster is one of the most famous and well-documented guitars in rock history.

tone.target: bright 70s arena crunch with lead bite
tone.profile: bright 70s arena crunch with lead bite
tone.summary: A classic Plexi/Marshall style chain using a Boost and OD pedal to achieve dry rhythm crunch, paired with the UK 45 amp model and Chorus/Digital Delay for anthemic leads.
corrections: drop chorus as a core tone

rig.name: Pink Floyd - Another Brick In The Wall, Part 2 - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide the initial dry rhythm crunch and bite (Plexi style).
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to emulate a slightly broken-in, mid-focused British overdrive suitable for the Plexi sound.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if more grit is needed.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use for extra grit if needed (kept off to maintain clarity).
blocks.gap: No dedicated distortion pedal is required as the Green OD provides sufficient crunch.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, mid-focused British Marshall/Plexi tone.
Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound.
Boost the upper mids and treble for lead bite and clarity.
blocks.gap: Used to manually sculpt the required 'bright upper mids' specified in the verdict.

blocks.purpose: Add the anthemic chorus feel for solo sections without excessive wash.
blocks.gap: The settings are dialed back to prevent 'chorus wash' while retaining the required effect.

blocks.purpose: Provide clear solo delay for lead lines (short delay setting).
blocks.gap: The short time and moderate feedback keep the effect supportive rather than ambient.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle depth and space without creating an 'ambient wash'.
blocks.gap: The mix is kept low to avoid excessive ambience.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for better realism and bite, especially in the upper mids.

proposals.reason: Enhance mid-range bite and vintage British tone.
